youtube.baslik: How short a silence can your ears detect? #shorts
youtube.aciklama: Gap detection is the most common measure of temporal resolution: a very short silence is placed in a noise, and the shortest gap that is detected is found. In young adults with normal hearing, this threshold is about 2 to 3 milliseconds in broadband noise; in older adults it is usually longer, even with a normal audiogram.
